## 2026-05-11 - Dynamic CSS Injection in ChartStyle Component
**Vulnerability:** Even internal-looking IDs (like those generated by React's `useId`) or theme/config-driven strings can be overridden via props (such as `<ChartContainer id="..." />`), leading to CSS rule breakout and arbitrary style injection when rendered within `<style dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: ... }} />`.
**Learning:** Raw string interpolation of prop values in dynamic `<style>` tags opens up pathways to CSS and potentially HTML/JS injection if user-controlled input makes its way to those props. Additionally, attribute selectors without quotes (e.g., `[data-chart=${id}]`) are especially susceptible to attribute selector breakout.
**Prevention:**
1. Always sanitize any dynamically interpolated strings (like IDs, config keys, and color values) in `<style>` blocks using restrictive alphanumeric/symbol whitelists and by blocking breakout characters like `;`, `{`, `}`, `[`, `]`, `"`, `'`, `<`, `>`, `\`, `:`, `@`.
2. Wrap attribute values in quotes inside CSS selector patterns, e.g., use `[data-chart="${cleanId}"]` instead of `[data-chart=${id}]`.
